==Education==
Fotis Kafatos graduated from the Lyceum Korais in Heraklion in 1958 and from [[Cornell University]] in 1961, where he was mentored by [[Thomas Eisner]]<ref>{{cite journal | last=Wright | first=Janet | title=Fotis Kafatos, chairman, scientific council of the European Research Council | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=440 | issue=7085 | year=2006 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nj7085-842a | doi-access=free | pages=842 | url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nj7085-842a.pdf | access-date=2025-03-26}}</ref> and assisted by the [[Fulbright Program]]{{citation needed|date=November 2017}} and a scholarship from [[Anne Gruner Schlumberger]]. He earned his [[PhD]] at Harvard in 1965 for research on [[entomology]], supervised by [[Carroll Williams]].<ref name=kafatosphd/>

==Research and career==
Fotis Kafatos was an influential Greek [[biologist]], having had a pivotal role in triggering the interest of the Greek government for Science, with the establishment of the Faculty of Biology in the [[University of Athens]], the Faculty of Biology in the [[University of Crete]] and the IMBB in [[Heraklion]].<ref name=imbbobit>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171122011827/http://www.imbb.forth.gr/news/FotisKafatosObituaryEN.pdf|archive-date=2017-11-22|url=http://www.imbb.forth.gr/news/FotisKafatosObituaryEN.pdf|title=Obituary Fotis Kafatos: 16th April 1940 – 18th November 2017|website=imbb.forth.gr|author=Anon|year=2017}}</ref>

At the beginning of his career, he contributed to the development of the [[complementary DNA]] (cDNA) [[cloning]] technology and worked on the mechanisms of cellular differentiation leading to the formation of the eggs in insects.<ref>[https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/query.fcgi?cmd=PureSearch&db=pubmed&details_term=kafatos%20fc%5BAuthor%5D PubMed references] ([https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/query.fcgi?cmd=PureSearch&db=pubmed&details_term=kafatos%20fc%5BAuthor%5D%20AND%20%22loattrfree%20full%20text%22%5Bsb%5D free full text references])</ref><ref>[http://www.jhsph.edu/publichealthnews/articles/2006/malaria_conference/kafatos_malaria.html Video and audio interview] with Kafatos at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health</ref> He has particular interest in [[malaria]] research and used his knowledge of the genetics and molecular biology of insects to understand how the insect vector copes with the [[Plasmodium]] parasite. He also participated in the sequencing of the genome of the mosquito ''[[Mosquito|Anopheles gambiae]]'' completed in [[2002 in science|2002]].<ref name="moz">{{Cite journal

He was assistant professor and later professor and chairman of the department of Cellular and Developmental Biology of Harvard University, professor of biology at the [[University of Athens]] and at the [[University of Crete]], director of the Institute of Molecular Biology and Biotechnology (IMBB)<ref name=imbb>{{cite web|url=http://www.imbb.forth.gr|website=imbb.forth.gr|title=Institute of Molecular Biology and Biotechnology}}</ref><ref name=imbbobit/> of the [[Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas]] in [[Heraklion]] and third director-general of the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] from 1993 to 2005.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Hoffmann | first1 = J. ===Awards and honours ===
Kafatos was a member of the US [[National Academy of Sciences]] since 1982 and of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences|American Academy]].{{citation needed|date=November 2017}}  He was elected a [[Foreign Member of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Louis|first1=Christos|last2=Goldsmith|first2=Marian R.|date=2020|title=Fotis C. Kafatos. 16 April 1940—18 November 2017|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=69|pages=273–289|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0010|s2cid=218685745|doi-access=free}}</ref> (ForMemRS) in 2003 and was also a member of the French [[Académie des Sciences]], the [[Pontifical Academy]] and the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO).<ref name=membo/> He was awarded the Louis-Jeantet 25th anniversary prize in 2008, the [[Robert Koch Medal]] in Gold in 2010, the BioMalPar.EviPalaR Lifetime Achievement Award in 2011, and the Leibnitz Medal in 2011.{{citation needed|date=November 2017}}  He was also a recipient of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]]{{citation needed|date=November 2017}} and of the [[Order of the Phoenix (Greece)|Greek Order of the Phoenix]],{{citation needed|date=November 2017}} as well as other awards and honorary degrees in Greece and elsewhere.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

==Personal life==
Fotis Kafatos was the son of Constantine and Helen Kafatos, had two brothers named Antonis and Menas, and lived until age 18 with his family in Heraklion, Crete, Greece. He married Sarah Niles in 1967 and they had two daughters, Helen and Zoe Myrto, and four grandchildren, George, Sophia, Arthur, and Anna.<ref>{{cite web | last1=Σουφλέρη | first1=Ιωάννα Α. | last2=Ιωακείμ | first2=Στράτος | last3=Αρχοντάκης | first3=Σοφοκλής | last4=Πρατικάκης | first4=Βαγγέλης | last5=Τσώλη | first5=Θεοδώρα Ν. | last6=Τσιλιόπουλος | first6=Ευθύμιος | last7=Αλεβίζου | first7=Έφη | last8=Ρούσσος | first8=Βιδιάνος | last9=Δαργάκης | first9=Νεκτάριος | title=Φώτης Καφάτος: Μια ζωή πρότυπο | website=in.gr | date=2020-11-18 | url=https://www.in.gr/2020/11/18/in-science/episthmes/fotis-kafatos-mia-zoi-protypo/ | language=el | access-date=2025-03-26}}</ref>
